decision_conditions: The development to which this permission relates must be begun not later than the expiration of three years beginning with the date of the decision notice. Reason: To comply with the provisions of S.51 of the Planning & Compulsory Purchase Act 2004.

The development hereby permitted shall be implemented in the accordance with the following approved plans:MWP2-ARP-XX-XX-SK-CF-00004 02MWP2-6 MWSIW-5 Flood Risk Assessment Rev 06, dated 10 March 2026Reason: For the avoidance of doubt and in the interests of proper planning.
The development hereby approved shall be implemented in accordance with the approved materials unless otherwise formally agreed.Reason: In the interest of visual amenity.

Prior to commencement of the development hereby permitted, a scheme to ensure protection and maintenance of the proposed flood defence barrier shall be submitted to, and approved in writing by, the local planning authority. The scheme shall be fully implemented and subsequently maintained, in accordance with the scheme's timing/ phasing arrangements, or within any other period as may subsequently be agreed, in writing, by the local planning authority.Reason: To ensure that the flood defence will remain functional throughout the lifetime of the development.

The development shall be carried out in accordance with the submitted flood risk assessment (MWP2-6 MWSIW-5 Flood Risk Assessment Rev 06, dated 10 March 2026) and the following measures it details:Installation of a flood barrier extending approximately 170m to the south of the Central Spine Road to a level of 10.95-10.99mAOD at the ramp.  These measures shall be retained and maintained thereafter.Reason: To ensure the overall Meridian Water flood alleviation scheme functions as designed, to reduce the risk of flooding to the Meridian Water development and its occupants and to meet the NPPF's requirements in relation to flood risk.

The existing towpath access point shall remain in situ unless and until either towpath access works as approved by permission 19/02717/RE3 have been completed and the access is available for use, or details of a suitable alternative towpath access have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved details.Reason: In the interest of equitable access for pedestrians.

Prior to first use, a Verification Report demonstrating that the approved Flood Risk measures have been fully implemented shall be submitted to the Local Planning Authority for approval in writing. This report must include:o	As built drawings of the Flood Barrier including level information (if appropriate)o	Photographs of the completed Flood Restraint Barriero	Any relevant certificates from manufacturers/ suppliers of any drainage featureso	A confirmation statement of the above signed by the site manager or similarReason : To ensure the sustainable management of water, minimise flood risk, minimise discharge of surface water outside of the curtilage of the property and ensure that the drainage system will remain functional throughout the lifetime of the development in accordance with Policy CP28 of the Core Strategy, DMD 59-62, and Policies SI12 & SI13 of the London Plan and the NPPF

Construction Management PlanNo development shall commence until a Construction Traffic Management Plan has been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority.  The statement should include:a)	Photographic condition survey of public carriageways, verges and footways in the vicinity of the site;b)	Map showing routeing of demolition and construction vehicles to/from the site;c)	Access arrangements to the site;d)	Wheel cleaning methodology and facilitiesReason: To ensure the implementation of the construction works does not lead to damage to the existing highway and to minimise disruption to neoghbouring properties.
